_comment: WC2026 ROUND OF 16 (bracket tie 93: winner of Brazil-Japan vs winner of Ivory Coast-Norway). KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Winner meets the Mexico-England winner in the quarter-finals. Routes: Brazil WON Group C (1-1 Morocco, 3-0 Haiti, 3-0 Scotland; 7 pts, GF 7 GA 1, rating 92) -- elite, a strong defence (GA 1, two clean sheets) -- then edged Japan 2-1 in the R32 (late winner, settled in 90'). Norway finished 2nd in Group I (4-1 Iraq, 3-1 Senegal, 1-4 France; 6 pts, GF 8 GA 6, GD +2, rating 81) -- ATTACKING (8 goals, Haaland) but LEAKY (shipped 4 to France, GA 6) -- then beat Ivory Coast 2-1 with a 93' winner in the R32. Class gap ~11 (92 vs 81) -> Brazil the clear favourite. BTTS RULE (v2) -- APPLIED WITH THE ELITE-STRIKER NUANCE: Brazil is a clear favourite (advancement ~74%, gap >6), which by default -> BTTS-No / favourite clean sheet. BUT the three prior BTTS misses (Bosnia, Algeria, Canada shut out) were all mid-tier underdogs WITHOUT an elite striker; Norway has HAALAND and a genuine attack (8 group goals) that can score on anyone. So the underdog haircut is applied only LIGHTLY (Norway 1.05 -> 0.98), landing BTTS ~54% (near-neutral, slight Yes) rather than a strong No -- honouring the rule's direction (Brazil's control pulls BTTS DOWN from the naive 56.7%) without disrespecting Haaland. This is an OPEN, higher-scoring tie (Brazil's attack vs a leaky Norway; Norway's attack vs a good-but-beatable Brazil D) -> a favourite+goals lean with a live BTTS, NOT a low-block grind. Brazil favoured to a comfortable-ish win, but Norway can score. Home = Brazil (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

meta.stakes: Single-elimination: level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties. Brazil the clear favourite (won Group C, rating 92, GA 1, beat Japan 2-1) vs an attacking-but-leaky Norway (2nd in Group I, rating 81, Haaland, beat Ivory Coast 2-1). An open, higher-scoring tie: Brazil favoured but Norway's elite attack keeps BTTS live (near-neutral, NOT a strong No) -- favourite+goals, not a grind.

home.name: Brazil
notes: Elite (rating 92), won Group C, GA 1; efficient attack (edged Japan 2-1). vs a leaky Norway (GA 6) -> should score freely. attack 1.15.
Strong defence (GA 1, two clean sheets) but Haaland is a real threat -> not a guaranteed shut-out. defense 0.88.
Clear favourite; open game vs an attacking side -> goals live, comfortable-ish but not a rout.

away.name: Norway
notes: ATTACKING with an ELITE striker (Haaland; 8 group goals, 3-1 Senegal). attack 0.85 -- only a LIGHT BTTS-rule haircut (NOT the hard trim used on mid-tier minnows): Norway can score on anyone, so BTTS kept near-neutral, not forced to No.
LEAKY (shipped 4 to France, GA 6) -> Brazil should break through. defense 1.05.
Clear underdog by class but a genuine attacking threat -> live BTTS, some ET/penalty tail.

_recal: First pass (BRA 1.95 / NOR 1.05) landed Brazil 57.6 / Draw 23.2 / Norway 19.2 vs market de-vig 58.6 / 23.4 / 18.0 (div 1.2, aligned) with BTTS 56.5%. Applied the BTTS rule DIRECTION but with the elite-striker nuance: a LIGHT trim NOR 1.05 -> 0.98 (and BRA 1.95 -> 1.98) pulls BTTS to ~54.5% (near-neutral) and lifts Brazil's clean sheet to 37.5%, while keeping 1X2 tight to the market (Brazil 59.9 / Draw 22.7 / Norway 17.4, div 1.4, MEDIUM). Did NOT force BTTS-No: Norway has Haaland (unlike the shut-out mid-tier underdogs Bosnia/Algeria/Canada). Advancement Brazil 73.8 / Norway 26.2; ET 22.7%, pens 10.6%.

_postmatch.result: Brazil 1-2 Norway. UPSET -- Norway ELIMINATE Brazil and advance to the quarter-finals (where they meet the Mexico-England winner). Haaland scored TWICE. Settled in 90'.
_postmatch.model_1x2: Brazil 59.9 / Draw 22.7 / Norway 17.4 (MEDIUM, 90'); advancement Brazil 73.8 / Norway 26.2
_postmatch.verdict: Wrong on the DELIVERABLE, right on the TEXTURE -- and the specific judgement call was vindicated. Brazil, the 73.8% favourite, was eliminated; Norway won 2-1 from the ~17.4% away-win / 26.2% advance branch. On the headline it is a MISS (❌): the favourite is out. BUT this is a PRICED upset, not a mispricing -- the market also had Norway ~18% to win in 90', and a ~1-in-4 underdog advancing is exactly what 26% means; it landed this time. Crucially, the ONE call that made this tie interesting was RIGHT: I explicitly REFUSED to apply the mechanical BTTS-No haircut because 'Norway has Haaland and can score on anyone', kept BTTS near-neutral (54.5%, slight Yes) and only trimmed Norway lightly -- and HAALAND SCORED TWICE. Had I blindly forced BTTS-No / hard-trimmed Norway (as for a mid-tier minnow), I would have compounded the error. The texture (BTTS-Yes, Norway scores) was dead-on; the elite-striker nuance in the BTTS rule earned its keep. Brazil's class got them one goal but their good-not-impenetrable defence (the reason I did not push clean sheet higher) was breached twice by a world-class striker.
_postmatch.lesson: TWO lessons, one reinforcing the method, one new: (1) VINDICATION of the BTTS elite-striker nuance -- do NOT hard-trim an underdog that has a genuine world-class attacking threat; Norway/Haaland is exactly the exception the rule carved out, and keeping BTTS live was correct (Haaland brace). Never mechanically apply the underdog-lambda haircut to a side with an elite striker. (2) NEW: an underdog with a genuine elite attacking threat carries real UPSET EQUITY, not just BTTS-Yes -- a Haaland can win the game OUTRIGHT, not merely score in a loss. A 'leaky underdog' with a top striker is more dangerous than rating alone implies; the advancement number (26%) was honest and market-aligned, but this class of underdog is where the favourite's ~25% elimination tail actually fires. Don't over-update the SIDE (Brazil 74% was correct process; ~1 in 4 of these goes to the underdog) -- but weight an elite-striker underdog toward the upper end of its upset range.
